about: Sfumato comes from Antica Erboristeria Cappelletti, a family herbalist’s firm that Giuseppe Cappelletti opened in Trento in 1906, gathering mountain herbs and selling them alongside imported spices. His tonics and syrups became amari, and for most of a century the shop stood on Trento’s Piazza Fiera. Today the fourth generation, Luigi and Maddalena Cappelletti, run production from Aldeno, about 20 kilometres south of the city among vineyards and apple orchards.

The house has made a rabarbaro, a rhubarb-based amaro, for nearly a hundred years. Sfumato is built on rhubarb root, which the importer describes as a variety grown in Trentino-Alto Adige and Veneto, joined by alpine herbs and berries, and everything is made in-house. The name plays on fumo, Italian for smoke, and on sfumato, the Renaissance painter’s technique of soft transitions between light and dark.

At 20% alcohol it is gentler than most amari. Expect a dark, smoky character with a woodsy bitterness from the herbs and a sweet lift of alpine berries. Bartenders reach for it in whiskey drinks and long serves with tonic or grapefruit soda, but it is just as good on its own, neat or over ice.
facts: Rhubarb root (rabarbaro) with alpine herbs and berries
Neat, on the rocks, or with tonic
